title: LAST — Recognition & Lipid Rescue
sources: Neal JM et al. ASRA Practice Advisory on Local Anesthetic Systemic Toxicity. Reg Anesth Pain Med 2023
Critical Vector — POCUS-Guided Nerve Block Procedural Reference

changelog.change: Source updated to the ASRA 2023 practice advisory (dosing unchanged: 1.5 mL/kg IBW bolus, 0.25 → 0.5 mL/kg/min infusion, ~12 mL/kg max); confirmed against the CV nerve-block reference.
Initial entry — shared component referenced from every nerve-block module.

summary: The one shared LAST reference, callable from every nerve-block entry. Recognition + the 20% lipid emulsion protocol.

items: CNS first: perioral numbness, metallic taste, tinnitus, agitation, confusion → seizure → coma
Then cardiovascular: hypertension/tachycardia → bradycardia, conduction block, ventricular arrhythmia, asystole
Onset is usually within minutes of injection but can be delayed up to ~60 min
Have a high index of suspicion after any large-volume or multi-level block (e.g. intercostals), or an unintended intravascular injection
Stop injecting. Call for help and the LAST rescue kit.
Airway: 100% oxygen, ventilate — hypoxia and acidosis worsen toxicity
Seizures: benzodiazepine first-line; avoid large doses of propofol in a haemodynamically unstable patient
ACLS with modifications: REDUCE the epinephrine dose to ≤ 1 mcg/kg boluses; AVOID vasopressin, calcium-channel blockers, beta-blockers, and local anesthetics (lidocaine, procainamide)

rows: 1.5 mL/kg lean body weight IV over ~1 min (≈ 100 mL in a 70 kg adult)
0.25 mL/kg/min (≈ 18 mL/min / ~1000 mL/h in a 70 kg adult)
Re-bolus once or twice and double the infusion to 0.5 mL/kg/min
For at least 10-15 min after haemodynamic stability is restored

body.text: Propofol is NOT a substitute for lipid emulsion — its lipid content is far too low and its cardiodepressant effect is harmful here. Consider early cardiopulmonary bypass / ECMO for refractory arrest.
